newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee retreats as specs sell in NY.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee retreats as specs sell in NY.

text.p: LIFFE coffee futures reversed an early uptrend to end Tuesday broadly lower, weighed down by sliding New York values on stop-loss selling and spec liquidation.
But traders in London said milder Brazilian weather was not the main factor behind New York's dive.
"It was just the specs who were pushing the market on either side and this hit stops all over the place," said one trader. "The volume is small and this probably exaggerated the move."
Another said: "Everybody knew there was no (Brazilian) frost but it didn't react until an hour later."
"The silly season is back," he said.
The London market went down on the back of the New York contract. "Otherwise, it could have got to a good close," the trader added.
LIFFE's July, which had firmed $70 at midsession, fell back to end the day $65 down at $1,825 per tonne.
September also gave up the day's advance to finish $75 down at $1,850 after climbing to a high of $2,005.
Traders said trade house Sucden was seen as a seller towards the close.
Overall volume was 7,766 lots, centred on the September contract.
New York's July arabica futures plunged to a session low of 225 cents a lb before trading 26.30 down at 227 cents at 1643 GMT.
"It was up 16 cents on the cold weather and there was no cold weather," said one U.S. dealer.
Private U.S. forecaster Weather Services Corp said on Tuesday high pressure that had brought cool weather to Brazil's coffee belt in the past few days was now heading out to sea.
A warming trend was expected to develop and continue through the end of the week.
Brazilian cooperatives said there were no reports of any frosts on coffee farms overnight. There were frosts in lower areas but they did not reach coffee plantations.
Technical analysts said coffee had tiptoed into slightly oversold ground after retracing about 61.8 percent of its move up last week.
But they warned that rigid bands of resistance loomed nearby, with strong September resistance seen between $2,025 and $2,300.
In options, a total of 1,181 lots changed hands. The September $1,800 puts saw a sizeable volume of 375 lots.
